translations.text: Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ by the will of God, according to the promise of life that is in Christ Jesus,
To Timothy, my beloved son: grace, mercy, and peace from God the Father and from Christ Jesus our Lord.
I thank God, whom I serve with a pure conscience as my ancestors did, as I constantly remember you in my prayers night and day.
I long to see you, remembering your tears, so that I may be filled with joy.
I remember the sincere faith that is in you, which first lived in your grandmother Lois and your mother Eunice, and I am convinced that it is in you as well.
For this reason I remind you to rekindle the gift of God that is in you through the laying on of my hands.
For God did not give us a spirit of timidity, but of power, love, and self-control.
Therefore, do not be ashamed of the testimony about our Lord, or of me, his prisoner, but share in suffering for the gospel according to the power of God,
who saved us and called us with a holy calling, not according to our works, but according to his own purpose and grace, which was given to us in Christ Jesus before time began.
But it has now been revealed through the appearing of our Savior Jesus Christ, who abolished death and brought life and immortality to light through the gospel,
for which I was appointed a preacher, an apostle, and a teacher of the Gentiles.
For this reason I also endure these sufferings, but I am not ashamed, because I know whom I have believed, and I am convinced that he is able to guard what I have entrusted to him until that day.
Keep the pattern of sound words that you heard from me, in the faith and love that are in Christ Jesus.
Guard the good thing entrusted to you through the Holy Spirit who lives in us.
Know this: all those who were in Asia have turned away from us, including Phygelus and Hermogenes.
May God grant mercy to the household of Onesiphorus, because he refreshed me many times and was not ashamed of my chains.
Instead, when he came to Rome, he searched very diligently for me and found me.
May the Lord grant him to find mercy from the Lord on that day. And you yourself know very well how much he served me in Ephesus.
But you, my son, be strengthened by the grace that is in Christ Jesus.
And what you heard from me in the presence of many witnesses, entrust to faithful people who will be able to teach others as well.
Share in suffering as a good soldier of Christ Jesus.
No one serving as a soldier here becomes entangled in the affairs of this world, so that he may please his commander.
And if someone competes as an athlete, he is not crowned unless he competes according to the rules.
And the farmer who labors ought to be the first to enjoy the harvest.
Understand what I am saying. May the Lord give you understanding in everything.
Remember Jesus Christ, raised from the dead, descended from David, according to my gospel,
for which I suffer even to the point of chains like a criminal. But the word of God is not bound.
Therefore I endure everything for the sake of the chosen, so that they too may attain the salvation that is in Christ Jesus, together with heavenly glory.
This saying is trustworthy: if we died with him, we will also live with him.
If we endure, we will also reign with him; and if we deny him, he too will deny us.
And if we are faithless, he remains faithful, for he cannot deny himself.
Remind them of these things, solemnly charging them before God not to quarrel over words, which serves no purpose and brings ruin to those who listen.
Make every effort to present yourself approved before God, a worker with no cause for shame, correctly handling the word of truth.
But keep away from profane and empty talk, for those who engage in it will advance further into ungodliness.
And their words will spread like cancer. Among them are Hymenaeus and Philetus.
They have strayed from the truth and say that the resurrection of the dead has already taken place, and they overturn the faith of some.
But God's firm foundation stands and bears this seal: “The Lord knows those who are his,” and, “Let everyone who names the name of the Lord turn away from wrongdoing.”
In a large house there are not only vessels of gold and silver, but also vessels of wood and clay. Some are for honorable use, and some for dishonorable use.
If anyone cleanses himself from such things, he will be a vessel for honorable use, made holy and useful to his Master, prepared for every good work.
But flee youthful desires, and pursue righteousness, faith, love, peace, and holiness, together with those who call on the name of the Lord with pure hearts.
But avoid foolish and ignorant disputes, knowing that they give rise to quarrels.
The Lord's servant must not quarrel, but must be gentle toward everyone, able to teach, and free from resentment,
correcting opponents with gentleness. Perhaps God will grant them repentance leading to knowledge of the truth,
and they will come to their senses and escape the devil's snares, having been captured by him to do his will.
Know this: in the last days, evil times will come.
For people will be lovers of themselves, lovers of money, proud, arrogant, blasphemous, disobedient to parents, ungrateful, unholy,
without devotion or compassion, slanderous, lacking self-control, fierce, and without love for what is good.
Traitors, reckless, arrogant, lovers of pleasure rather than lovers of God.
They will have the outward form of godliness but will have denied its power. Turn away from them.
For among them are those who go from house to house and take captive women burdened with sins and driven by various desires,
who are always learning but never attain knowledge of the truth.
Just as Jannes and Jambres opposed Moses, so these people oppose the truth: people whose minds are corrupted and who are unfit as regards the faith.
But they will never advance any further, for their foolishness will become evident to everyone, just as the foolishness of those men did.
But you followed my teaching, my guidance, my willingness, my faith, my patience, my love, my endurance,
my persecutions and sufferings, such as those that befell me in Antioch, Iconium, and Lystra. What persecutions I endured! And the Lord rescued me from them all.
And all who wish to live godly lives in Christ Jesus will face persecution.
But evil people and sorcerers will go from bad to worse, being deceived and deceiving others.
But you must remain firm in what you learned and came to believe, knowing from whom you learned it.
For from childhood you have known the sacred writings, which can make you wise for salvation through faith in Christ Jesus.
All Scripture is inspired by God and useful for teaching, for rebuke, for correction, and for instruction in righteousness,
so that the person of God may be complete, equipped for every good work.
I give this solemn charge before God and Jesus Christ, who will judge the living and the dead at his appearing and in his kingdom:
Preach the word; be ready in season and out of season; rebuke, reprimand, and encourage with all patience and teaching.
For a time will come when they will not listen to sound teaching, but according to their own desires they will gather teachers for themselves to satisfy their itching ears.
They will turn their ears away from the truth and fall into myths.
But you must remain watchful in everything, endure hardship, do the work of an evangelist, and fulfill your ministry.
For I am now being offered, and the time of my departure has arrived.
I have fought the good fight, finished the race, and kept the faith.
From now on, the crown of righteousness is kept for me, which the Lord, the righteous Judge, will award me on that day—not only to me, but also to all who have loved his appearing.
Make haste to come to me soon, for Demas left me, loved the world, and went to Thessalonica.
Crescens went to Galilee, Titus to Dalmatia. Only Luke is with me.
Take Mark and bring him with you, for he is useful to me in ministry.
I sent Tychicus to Ephesus.
I left the cloak in Troas with Carpus. When you come, bring it, and the books, especially the manuscripts.
Alexander caused me much suffering. May the Lord repay him according to his deeds.
You too must guard yourself against him, for he strongly opposed our words.
At my first hearing, no one stood by me, but everyone abandoned me. May this not be counted against them.
But the Lord helped me and strengthened me, so that through me the proclamation might be firmly established and all the Gentiles might hear it. And I was rescued from the lion’s mouth.
May the Lord rescue me from every evil work and bring me safely into his kingdom in heaven. To him be glory forever and ever. Amen.
Greet Prisca and Aquila and the household of Onesiphorus.
Erastus remained in Corinth. I left Trophimus sick in Miletus.
Make haste to come before winter. Eubulus, Pudens, Linus, Claudia, and all the brothers greet you.

The Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit. Grace be with you. The second letter to Timothy, who was the first ordained bishop of the church of the Ephesians, was written from Rome when Paul stood for the second time at a hearing before Nero, emperor of Rome.
